description: In an interview recorded at UCF’s John C. Hitt Library on September 11, 2026, the speaker introduces herself as Sharika Garner and identifies the interview as part of the Night Tales Project. Garner recalls being a senior at University High School in Orlando, across the street from UCF, on September 11, 2001. She describes arriving early for the senior class panoramic photograph, then waiting in the courtyard before walking to a class where students were watching television coverage of the World Trade Center attack. Confused by the quiet and events at school, she called her father, who told her she could go home; she later recalls the long line of parents signing students out. Garner says she stayed at school until the end of the day and understood the magnitude of the events more fully after returning home and finding that her father had left work early. The account is a personal recollection of school experiences and television news coverage, with no claim that Garner was physically present at an attack site.

So on September 11th, I was a senior in high school. I went to high school right across the street from UCF. I don't know if this is something that folks still do, but at the time, every member of the senior class would go to the gym and take a panoramic photo that would end up in the yearbook and the office, and, like, you could buy your own copy and things of that sort. I normally did not have a first period, but because of our senior class photo, I went to school early that day. Also, I went to a school that had about 5,000 students, and so we had about eight or nine hundred students

in our senior class. So we all lined up, gathered into the gym to take our senior photo. It probably took about 20 minutes to take the photo, and then because I was a senior class officer, after everyone left, I stayed behind to help clean up. So about 10 or 20 minutes after everyone left, I went out to the courtyard because, again, I did not have a first period. So it was about 8:50, 9 o'clock in the morning, and I went out to the courtyard to wait for the bell to ring to go to second period. So because this was 2001, I did not have a cell phone. Well, I had a cell phone, but it didn't have the time. I think it was off. It was like a very large cell phone that you really only used in emergencies. And so I was sitting on the bench just waiting for the bell to ring, and the bell never rang. It was very, very quiet. I was super confused because I had kind of, like, dazed out, and I wasn't

really sure what time it was or how long I had been sitting on this bench. And so I was like, I think maybe I missed the bell, which I don't know why I missed the bell. I thought I missed the bell because class change would have been 5,000 students in the hallway, so I don't think there's any way that I could have missed the bell to head to second period. But I started walking to my second period. Our school was very large, so it had two campuses, so I had to walk across the street to our second campus. And I got to my second period, or my first period of the day, and I walked into class and none of the people were familiar because the bell had not rang to go to second period. So these were students who were still in that teacher's first period, and they were watching TV. And so I walked in and I was like, These students are not very scholarly because they're in here watching TV.

Everyone was quiet. I was super confused about what was going on. And so my teacher, who was a history teacher, was like, They hit the World Trade Center. A plane hit the World Trade Center. And I was like, What does that mean? What are we talking about? I haven't heard anything. I just got here. And so I just remember sitting in that classroom for about an hour just watching the news coverage over and over again. And then I just couldn't sit there anymore. So I told my teacher that I was going to go to PE. Because my other class of the day was PE, and so I went to the locker room, and I was the only person in there. So everywhere that I was going that day, I was really kind of the only person around, and so I was very confused about what was happening. So I remember that I called my dad.
